transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I... I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's getting so bad. Like, my kitchen table right now? It is completely covered with my husband’s appointment papers. Frank has been seeing a new cardiologist—Dr. Miller, over on 4th street? Such a nice man, but his waiting room is always freezing. I always tell Frank to bring a sweater, but does he listen? 

Anyway, Frank's papers are there, along with all these church flyers. I usually help with the spring bazaar, I make a lovely lemon pound cake, though I couldn't find decent lemons at the grocery store this week... they were all so hard. Oh, and the senior-center notes are piled up there too, and just... half-finished lists everywhere. I sit down at that table, and I look at it all, and I just don't know which thing to do first. I just sit there. And then I look at the clock and the whole entire day is gone. I just don't know where the time goes.
When you find yourself unable to start those tasks, is it because you feel overwhelmed by the clutter, or is it because you are having trouble remembering what those papers are for?

I'm not really sure... I mean, I know what the papers are, mostly. Like Frank's medical bills, I know those are for him. He really shouldn't be eating so much salt with his heart the way it is, but he just loves those big soft pretzels. You know, the kind they sell at the mall? We used to get them all the time when the girls were little and we'd go back-to-school shopping. The mall used to be so lovely back then. Now half the stores are just boarded up. It’s such a shame, really. I needed to buy a new pair of walking shoes last month and I had to drive all the way out to the county line just to find a place that sells decent arch support. The salesman was very young, didn't know a thing about proper sizing, kept trying to put me in these neon pink sneakers... 

But, oh dear, what was your question? I'm sorry. The papers on the table? I just... I look at it all and I really don't know why I can't start. I just don't know.
Beyond the difficulty with your tasks, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless lately?

Sad? Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I get terribly frustrated with myself, but I wouldn't say hopeless. Now, my neighbor Doris, she gets very down. She was just telling me over the fence on Tuesday... or was it Wednesday? No, Tuesday, because Tuesday is when the street sweeper comes by. They make such a terrible racket, and honestly, they don't even really pick up the leaves. 

The big oak tree in our front yard drops leaves all year round, it seems. Frank used to rake them every single weekend, but his back just can't take it anymore. We tried hiring the Henderson boy from down the street to do it, but teenagers these days, they just stare at their phones. I saw him standing right in the middle of the lawn, rake in one hand, just tapping away on that little screen with his thumb. I don't even know what they look at on those things all day long. My granddaughter showed me how to look at pictures of recipes on my iPad, which is nice, I suppose, but the screen gets so smudgy with fingerprints. I tried wiping it with a paper towel and Frank said I was going to scratch the glass... 

Oh, I'm sorry. Did I even answer your question? I just get to talking and my mind goes right out the window. What did you ask me?
Have you always struggled with this kind of disorganization and difficulty getting started on tasks since you were much younger, or is this a new problem that has developed more recently?

Oh, heavens, no, it's not new at all. It’s always been this way. Even when I was just a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was a bright child but just so careless. I was always forgetting my reading books or leaving my homework at home, and they constantly had to remind me to finish my seatwork before I was ever allowed to go outside for recess. 

We had the most wonderful playground at my elementary school, though. It had one of those giant metal merry-go-rounds. You just don't see those anymore, they say they're too dangerous for children now. My brother Tommy flew right off one once and tore a huge hole in the knee of his brand new corduroy pants. My mother was just livid because she had just bought them from the Sears Roebuck catalog. Oh, the Sears catalog... we used to wait for the big Christmas wish book to arrive in the mail and we'd sit on the rug and circle all the toys we wanted with a red crayon. I think I still have a tin of Tommy's old crayons somewhere up in the attic. Or maybe it's down in the basement? Though the basement gets terribly damp in the spring, I keep telling Frank we need to have a plumber look at the pipes down there before all our old photo boxes get ruined... 

Oh dear. I've done it again, haven't I? Did that answer your question about the pipes, or... what were we talking about?
